newsitem.title: FRANCE: Outlook for UK joining euro favourable - Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: Outlook for UK joining euro favourable - Arthuis.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Wednesday that the latest moves by the new British Labour government appeared to show a willingness to join the euro.
Commenting on plans to make the Bank of England more independent, he said the new British administration "wanted to prepare for joining the euro, they would not do otherwise," he told reporters.

"I have the feeling that Mr Tony Blair and his Chancellor of the Exchequer (Gordon Brown) are leaning in the direction of membership in monetary union, not the least because the Chancellor promised to change the status of the Bank of England to take it, in a way, towards the model of the Bank of France," Arthuis said at a news conference.
"The fact that he raised interest rates to hold inflation to a rate that, it seems, is compatible with the (Maastricht treaty) convergence criteria is a promising sign."

Britain's new Labour government ordered on Tuesday an increase in official interest rates to 6.25 percent from 6.0 percent and gave the British central bank operational independence to set monetary policy.
